key_insight: Successive screenshots repeat much of the same visual content, suggesting that real-time visual indexing need not encode every frame from scratch. StreamEmbed targets this redundancy to make screen history searchable.
problem_solved: Screen history must be indexed as screenshots arrive. OCR is fast but misses visual information, while full visual encoding takes over two seconds, creating a bottleneck for real-time retrieval.
method: Treat incoming screenshots as a continuous indexing stream rather than a static, offline collection.
Exploit repeated pixels within and across screenshots to reduce redundant visual computation.
The provided abstract is truncated; the specific reuse mechanism and retrieval pipeline are not described.
impact: Efficient visual indexing could give people and AI agents searchable screen memory without relying solely on text. The excerpt motivates lower processing latency but provides no measured speedup or retrieval results.
visual_elements: Screenshot timeline with unchanged regions shaded and changed regions highlighted.
Pipeline diagram: incoming screenshots → visual encoding → searchable index → retrieval.
Comparison cards: OCR indexing—fast but text-limited; full visual encoding—visually rich but over two seconds.

paper_title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
paper_authors: Dayoon Ko, Yichuan Wang, Soyeong Jeong, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Gunhee Kim
